title: Tables
summary: The one container type in Luau. A table maps keys to values — used as arrays, dictionaries, objects, inventories, config files, and module namespaces.

syntax: local dict = { coins = 50, gems = 2 }     -- dictionary part
local mixed = {1, 2, name = "x"}           -- both at once (valid but be careful)

details.heading: Reading and writing
details.body: `t[key]` reads, `t[key] = value` writes. String keys can use dot sugar: `dict.coins`. Any value except nil can be a key (numbers, strings, booleans, even other tables).

details.heading: Length operator
details.body: `#t` gives the length of the *array part* — the run of consecutive integer keys starting at 1. It does NOT count dictionary entries, and behaves unpredictably with holes (nils in the middle).

details.heading: Tables are references
details.body: Assigning `local b = t` copies the *reference*, not the contents. Both names point at the same table; changes through one are visible through the other. Use `table.clone(t)` for a shallow copy.

explanation.whatItIs: A table is a collection of key→value pairs. If you need to store more than one thing — a list of players, an inventory, settings, an object with fields — you reach for a table. Arrays and dictionaries are just two flavors of the same thing.
explanation.whyItExists: Luau intentionally ships one flexible container instead of separate array/dictionary/object types. Less to learn; everything composes.
whenToUse: Objects and modules (tables of functions) — see metatables and modules
whenNotToUse: For a single value you don't need a table
Avoid mixing array and dictionary styles in one table unless you know what you're doing — `#t` only understands the array part
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local player = {
    name = "Raanis",     -- dictionary part
    level = 12,
}
local scores = {97, 45, 88}   -- array part: keys are 1, 2, 3

player.name       --> "Raanis"   (key lookup)
scores[2]         --> 45         (index lookup)
#scores           --> 3
```
tips: Build large strings with a table + `table.concat`, not `..` in a loop
`table.freeze(t)` makes a table read-only — great for constants/config
commonMistakes: Starting array indices at 0 — Luau arrays start at 1
Expecting `pairs` to return keys in insertion order — it doesn't guarantee any order
Thinking `local b = t` makes an independent copy

examples.title: An inventory as a dictionary
examples.code:
local inventory = {
    sword = 1,
    potion = 5,
}

inventory.potion = inventory.potion - 1     -- use one
inventory.shield = 1                        -- add new key

for item, count in inventory do   -- Luau: pairs is optional in generic for
    print(item, count)
end

examples.title: Tables are references
examples.code:
local original = { coins = 100 }
local alias = original        -- NOT a copy!

alias.coins = 0
print(original.coins)         --> 0  (same table)

local copy = table.clone(original)
copy.coins = 999
print(original.coins)         --> 0  (clone is independent... shallowly)
examples.commonMistake: `table.clone` is shallow: nested tables inside are still shared. Deep-copy manually when needed.
